href=\"#architecture\"\u003eArchitecture\u003c/a\u003e\n\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAgentConnect is an open-source platform where teams and multiple AI agents work\ntogether across Slack, Telegram, Discord, Lark, GitHub, GitLab, and Linear.\nBring Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, DeepSeek, Pi, or any ACP-compatible agent\ninto the conversations and workflows your team already has open.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eGive each agent a role, then let people and agents collaborate in shared\nconversations. Agents can call one another and remember what they learn, and\nwork can begin from a message, issue, pull request, webhook, or schedule.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp align=\"center\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n  \u003ca href=\"https://agentconnect.md\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003e\u003cimg src=\"/agentconnect-md/agentconnect/raw/main/docs/assets/agents-across-channels.png\" alt=\"People and agents working together in Slack, Telegram, and Discord conversations and in a GitHub pull request review\" width=\"880\" style=\"max-width: 100%;\"\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\n\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp align=\"center\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n  \u003csub\u003e▶ \u003ca href=\"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KA7xHF5JbJc\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eWatch the two-minute introduction\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/sub\u003e\n\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eWhy AgentConnect?\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-why-agentconnect\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Why AgentConnect?\" href=\"#why-agentconnect\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAI agents are getting better at doing work. The harder problem is making\nmultiple agents work well with a team—and with each other.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eMost agents still live like personal tools, in one person's terminal. Teammates\ncan't see what an agent is doing, can't take over a session, can't review its\noutput, and the context it builds stays on one laptop. So every team writes the\nsame glue: message channels, cron jobs, credential handling, context stitching.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAgentConnect turns that glue into a platform.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eUse cases\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTriage issues together.\u003c/strong\u003e People and agents investigate in one shared\nthread, bring in the right specialists, and keep the fix and verification\nvisible from start to finish.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSupport across trusted workspaces.\u003c/strong\u003e Start a support conversation in\nTelegram, involve engineering from a trusted Slack workspace, and return the\nresolution where the conversation began.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRun recurring operations.\u003c/strong\u003e Start work from a schedule or webhook, bring\nexceptions into a shared conversation, and keep the human decision visible.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eKeep private forks current.\u003c/strong\u003e Subscribe to upstream changes through GitHub,\na GitHub subscription in Slack, webhooks, or schedules. Let agents assess the\nimpact, prepare and test relevant updates, and bring them to the team for\nreview.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRun customized code review.\u003c/strong\u003e Run a general reviewer on every pull request,\nthen bring in architecture or security reviewers only when a change needs\nthem. Each reviewer can use its own model, instructions, repository access,\ntools, and sandbox policy.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eFeatures\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-features\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Features\" href=\"#features\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eWork as one team, on any runtime.\u003c/strong\u003e Create agents with different roles and\nlet them call on one another, while people follow along in the conversations\nwhere the work happens. Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, DeepSeek, Pi, and any\nother ACP-compatible runtime run side by side, and changing one does not\nrebuild the workflow around it.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eKeep work where it happens.\u003c/strong\u003e Link agents to bots in Slack, Telegram,\nDiscord, and Lark, or to repositories, issues, and workflows on GitHub,\nGitLab, and Linear.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eChoose the right agent for every job.\u003c/strong\u003e Configure each agent's runtime,\nmodel, workspace, tools, and machine independently.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCarry context forward.\u003c/strong\u003e Give each agent its own memory and skills, and\npublish reviewed\n\u003ca href=\"https://docs.agentconnect.md/docs/knowledge\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eKnowledge\u003c/a\u003e that every agent can\nfind on demand.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSet clear boundaries.\u003c/strong\u003e Decide who can see each agent and session, which\nrepositories and tools it may use, and which other agents it may call.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eStay in control.\u003c/strong\u003e Self-host the Apache-2.0 stack and keep agent execution\nand workspaces in the environment you operate.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eOne place to operate your whole fleet—agents, sessions, schedules, tools,\nknowledge, and daemons:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp align=\"center\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n  \u003ca href=\"https://app.agentconnect.md\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003e\u003cimg src=\"/agentconnect-md/agentconnect/raw/main/docs/assets/console-agents.gif\" alt=\"AgentConnect console: touring the Agents, Sessions, Schedules, Tools \u0026amp; Skills, Knowledge, and Daemons views\" width=\"880\" data-animated-image=\"\" style=\"max-width: 100%;\"\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\n\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp align=\"center\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n  \u003csub\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDon't just take our word for it. the daemon/relay data\nplane. Apart from explicitly approved organization knowledge and bounded skill\nbundles, the Control Plane stores coordination metadata—not message bodies,\nattachment bytes, pending Dream proposals, or ACP session streams. <p dir="auto">AgentConnect is an open-source platform where teams and multiple AI agents work
together across Slack, Telegram, Discord, Lark, GitHub, GitLab, and Linear.
Bring Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, DeepSeek, Pi, or any ACP-compatible agent
into the conversations and workflows your team already has open.</p>
<p dir="auto">Give each agent a role, then let people and agents collaborate in shared
conversations. Agents can call one another and remember what they learn, and
work can begin from a message, issue, pull request, webhook, or schedule.</p>
<p align="center" dir="auto">
  <a href="https://agentconnect.md" rel="nofollow"><img src="/agentconnect-md/agentconnect/raw/main/docs/assets/agents-across-channels.png" alt="People and agents working together in Slack, Telegram, and Discord conversations and in a GitHub pull request review" width="880" style="max-width: 100%;"></a>
</p>

  <sub>▶ <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KA7xHF5JbJc" rel="nofollow"><strong>Watch the two-minute introduction</strong></a></sub>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Why AgentConnect?</h2><a id="user-content-why-agentconnect" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Why AgentConnect?" href="#why-agentconnect"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">AI agents are getting better at doing work. The harder problem is making
multiple agents work well with a team—and with each other.</p>
<p dir="auto">Most agents still live like personal tools, in one person's terminal. Teammates
can't see what an agent is doing, can't take over a session, can't review its
output, and the context it builds stays on one laptop. So every team writes the
same glue: message channels, cron jobs, credential handling, context stitching.</p>
<p dir="auto">AgentConnect turns that glue into a platform.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Use cases</h3><a id="user-content-use-cases" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Use cases" href="#use-cases"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Teams use it to:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Triage issues together.</strong> People and agents investigate in one shared
thread, bring in the right specialists, and keep the fix and verification
visible from start to finish.</li>
<li><strong>Support across trusted workspaces.</strong> Start a support conversation in
Telegram, involve engineering from a trusted Slack workspace, and return the
resolution where the conversation began.</li>
<li><strong>Run recurring operations.</strong> Start work from a schedule or webhook, bring
exceptions into a shared conversation, and keep the human decision visible.</li>
<li><strong>Keep private forks current.</strong> Subscribe to upstream changes through GitHub,
a GitHub subscription in Slack, webhooks, or schedules. Let agents assess the
impact, prepare and test relevant updates, and bring them to the team for
review.</li>
<li><strong>Run customized code review.</strong> Run a general reviewer on every pull request,
then bring in architecture or security reviewers only when a change needs
them. Each reviewer can use its own model, instructions, repository access,
tools, and sandbox policy.</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Features</h3><a id="user-content-features" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Features" href="#features"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Work as one team, on any runtime.</strong> Create agents with different roles and
let them call on one another, while people follow along in the conversations
where the work happens. Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, DeepSeek, Pi, and any
other ACP-compatible runtime run side by side, and changing one does not
rebuild the workflow around it.</li>
<li><strong>Keep work where it happens.</strong> Link agents to bots in Slack, Telegram,
Discord, and Lark, or to repositories, issues, and workflows on GitHub,
GitLab, and Linear.</li>
<li><strong>Choose the right agent for every job.</strong> Configure each agent's runtime,
model, workspace, tools, and machine independently.</li>
<li><strong>Carry context forward.</strong> Give each agent its own memory and skills, and
publish reviewed
<a href="https://docs.agentconnect.md/docs/knowledge" rel="nofollow">Knowledge</a> that every agent can
find on demand.</li>
<li><strong>Set clear boundaries.</strong> Decide who can see each agent and session, which
repositories and tools it may use, and which other agents it may call.</li>
<li><strong>Stay in control.</strong> Self-host the Apache-2.0 stack and keep agent execution
and workspaces in the environment you operate.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">One place to operate your whole fleet—agents, sessions, schedules, tools,

<p dir="auto">Start the Web console, Control Plane, Relay, and PostgreSQL with Docker Compose:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="git clone https://github.com/agentconnect-md/agentconnect.git
cd agentconnect
docker compose up -d --pull always"><pre>git clone https://github.com/agentconnect-md/agentconnect.git
<span class="pl-c1">cd</span> agentconnect
docker compose up -d --pull always</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Open <code>http://localhost:3000</code>, add a daemon from the console, run its generated
command, and create your first agent. The default stack listens only on
<code>127.0.0.1</code> and uses local no-auth mode for evaluation.</p>

<p dir="auto">The official Helm chart is published on every release under the same version
number as the release itself:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="oci://ghcr.io/agentconnect-md/charts/agentconnect"><pre class="notranslate"><code>oci://ghcr.io/agentconnect-md/charts/agentconnect

<p dir="auto">A cluster install is three steps — create the namespace and its secrets, write
the values file for your deployment, then install — so follow the
<a href="https://docs.agentconnect.md/docs/kubernetes-deployment" rel="nofollow">Kubernetes guide</a>
rather than a one-liner. The chart source lives in
<a href="/agentconnect-md/agentconnect/blob/main/charts/agentconnect"><code>charts/agentconnect</code></a>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Configure the deployment</h3><a id="user-content-configure-the-deployment" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Configure the deployment" href="#configure-the-deployment"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Setup Server</strong> runs in the base stack at <code>http://localhost:8091</code>, always on
loopback. It configures browser authentication through Logto, the deployment's
GitHub, Slack, Google, and Lark / Feishu apps, the sign-in methods you show, and
preset-agent behavior. Deployment topology — images, ports, public URLs,
database and bootstrap secrets — stays in <code>compose.env</code> or your Helm values.</p>
<p dir="auto">Prefer to be walked through it? This repository ships a <strong>setup skill</strong> at
<code>.claude/skills/agentconnect-setup</code>, also exposed at <code>.agents/skills</code>, so Claude
Code, Codex, and other agent harnesses pick it up. Open your coding agent in the
checkout and ask it to set up AgentConnect: it runs the guide as an interactive
tutorial and verifies each checkpoint before continuing, and never asks you to
paste secrets into chat.</p>
<p dir="auto">For authentication, public URLs, Linux sandbox requirements, provider apps,
image pinning, secrets, and optional Mem0 configuration, follow the
<a href="https://docs.agentconnect.md/docs/oss-get-started" rel="nofollow">AgentConnect OSS guide</a>.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Architecture</h2><a id="user-content-architecture" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Architecture" href="#architecture"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="/agentconnect-md/agentconnect/blob/main/docs/designs/architecture.svg"><img src="/agentconnect-md/agentconnect/raw/main/docs/designs/architecture.svg" alt="AgentConnect message paths between the platforms, daemons, relay, and Control Plane" style="max-width: 100%;"></a></p>
<markdown-accessiblity-table><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Component</th>
<th>Responsibility</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><strong>Daemon</strong></td>
<td>Runs placed agents over daemon-owned ACP, owns workspaces and session state, maintains direct platform connections and schedules, and sends model-provider traffic directly</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Relay</strong> (optional)</td>
<td>Accepts callback-based ingress and webchat, proxies centrally managed MCP and OpenConnector access, and forwards message ingress directly to the owning daemon without durable storage</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Control Plane + Web UI</strong></td>
<td>Manages authentication, configuration, placement, permissions, metadata, and observability; stores explicitly approved organization knowledge/skill revisions and otherwise proxies bounded daemon reads on demand</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>
<p dir="auto">Live platform messages and ACP update streams stay on the daemon/relay data
plane. Apart from explicitly approved organization knowledge and bounded skill
bundles, the Control Plane stores coordination metadata—not message bodies,
attachment bytes, pending Dream proposals, or ACP session streams. If it is
temporarily unavailable, established sessions and daemon-local schedules
continue; new assignments and configuration changes resume after reconnection.</p>
<p dir="auto">See the
<a href="/agentconnect-md/agentconnect/blob/main/docs/designs/architecture.md">architecture design</a> for the
complete message paths, trust boundaries, and failure model.</p>
